test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 30 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Under Liberalisation in 1991, several foreign exchange reforms were initiated. In this context, which of the following is true for devaluation of domestic currency?

options.text: Fixing the domestic currency to all foreign currency
Lowering the value of foreign currency in relation to domestic currency
Increasing value of domestic currency in relation to foreign currency
Lowering the value of domestic currency in relation to foreign currency

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lowering the value of domestic currency in relation to foreign currency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devaluation of currency** refers to the deliberate downward adjustment of a nation's currency relative to foreign currencies.
 
• It is typically carried out by the **government or central bank** to make exports cheaper and imports more expensive.
 
• Under the **Liberalisation policy of 1991**, India adopted economic reforms, including the devaluation of the Indian Rupee to address the **balance of payments crisis**.
 
• Devaluation increases the competitiveness of a country's exports, making them more attractive in the **global market**.
 
• This step also discourages imports by making them more expensive, thereby helping in reducing the **trade deficit**.
 
• Devaluation is different from depreciation, which is a natural decline in the value of a currency due to **market forces**.
 
• For India in 1991, the devaluation was an important measure to secure international aid and to stabilize its **financial condition.**
 
• The devaluation of the Indian Rupee was followed by other reforms such as industrial delicensing and foreign investment liberalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fixing the domestic currency to all foreign currency**__

 __
 
• Fixing the domestic currency to foreign currency is referred to as a **pegged exchange rate system**, where a country fixes its currency value to another currency or a basket of currencies.
 
• This method is not related to devaluation, as devaluation implies a reduction in the fixed value, whereas pegging involves stabilization.
 
• Examples include countries like **China** that have historically pegged their currency to the US Dollar.
 
 
 
• **Increasing value of domestic currency in relation to foreign currency**__
 
 
• This refers to the **appreciation of domestic currency**, which is the opposite of devaluation.
 
• Appreciation occurs due to market forces such as increased demand for a country's goods, services, or currency.
